title: Employment of Ex-offenders at Key Installations Such as Jurong Island and Changi Airport
what_it_is: Employment of Ex-offenders at Key Installations Such as Jurong Island and Changi Airport

sections.label: Ex-offenders at key installations
sections.summary: An MP asks whether any policy bars ex-offenders from entering or working at key installations like Jurong Island and Changi Airport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Government has any policy prohibiting ex-offenders from entering or being employed at key installations, such as Jurong Island and Changi Airport; (b) if so, what categories of offences are covered by this policy; (c) what conditions need to be met before the prohibition lapses; and (d) if not, how many ex-offenders have been employed at these key installations over the past five years.

sections.label: YRSG registered employers
sections.summary: As at end of February 2022, about 5,800 employers are registered with YRSG offering ex-offender employment, with over 2,700 job listings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As at end of February 2022, about 5,800 employers are registered with YRSG to offer employment to ex-offenders, with over 2,700 job listings.

sections.label: Ex-offenders securing jobs
sections.summary: Of these, over 2,700, or 94%, secured jobs successfully.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Of these, over 2,700, or 94% of them, secured jobs successfully.

sections.label: Risk matrix, not blanket ban
sections.summary: The speaker says a risk matrix approach is used, and clarifies the question sought to know if a blanket prohibition exists for ex-offenders entering these facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If they say, well, it depends on the offence, then, in principle, they agree with the approach taken by the Government and that is what we do now, because we adopt a risk matrix approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Just to respond to the Minister's point, the intent of my question was to understand if there was a blanket prohibition for ex-offenders entering to these facilities as, say, delivery drivers or to be employed in these facilities.

sections.label: Assisting while protecting vulnerable
sections.summary: The Government is focused on assisting but is also clear-eyed about making sure the vulnerable are protected.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Government is very focused in trying to assist, but we are also very clear-eyed about trying to make sure that the vulnerable are protected.
